sources.citation: Asonye, Emma, Ezinne Emma-Asonye & Mary Edward. 2018. Deaf in Nigeria: A Preliminary Survey of Isolated Deaf Communities. SAGE Open 8(2).
sources.note: Only other published work by the documenting team on Nigerian village Deaf communities; CC-BY open access but the publisher site blocked automated download. Would at most confirm the community's existence and signer numbers; very unlikely to contain any prosodic statement (survey, not description).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page maga1273 'Magajingari Sign Language' and bib record 656877 (https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/maga1273;https://glottolog.org/resource/reference/id/656877).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: one reference (Asonye & Akpan 2021, minimal); comment 'Presumed independent'; AES 'shifting'. No descriptive grammar, sketch or phonology listed.

sources.citation: Asonye, Emma & Aniefon Daniel Akpan. 2021. Gesture in numerals in three indigenous Nigerian Sign Languages. Paper (27 slides) presented at the 7th International Conference on Language Documentation and Conservation (ICLDC 7), 6 March 2021. ScholarSpace, University of Hawai'i at Manoa,http://hdl.handle.net/10125/74462.(Glottolog ref 656877, listed by Glottolog as a minimal description; the only Glottolog reference for maga1273.)
sources.note: Nothing. Slides treat numeral signs (dominant fingers, handshapes, palm orientation) in Magajin Gari SL (MgSL), Ibokun SL and Akure SL; two short paragraphs locate the Magajin Gari Deaf community in northern Kaduna. No prosody, no stress, no phonology beyond handshape features of numerals; a full-text search for stress/accent returns zero hits.

sources.citation: Save the Deaf and Endangered Languages Initiative (S-DELI, Emma Asonye) documentation corpus of Magajin Gari Sign Language (video recordings referred to in the ICLDC 7 slides); any ELAR/other archive deposit if one exists.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The slides refer to video data 'documented' in Magajin Gari; an archive deposit or later write-up by Asonye's group would be the only conceivable place for a structural (phonological) description. s-deli.org returned an expired-certificate error; existence of a deposit not verified.
